topic: What If No One Could Speak?

character_sheet_descriptions.man_turnaround: Stylized 3D adult man in his 30s, short dark brown hair, light stubble, teal crew-neck t-shirt, grey jeans, white sneakers, expressive oversized eyes, smooth plasticine skin with subtle subsurface scattering.
character_sheet_descriptions.larynx_cross_section_turnaround: 3D medical model of the human larynx, front view and top-down cutaway view showing two pearly-white vocal folds over a pink glossy airway, semi-translucent cartilage, bright interior lighting.
character_sheet_descriptions.brain_language_turnaround: 3D medical model of a semi-translucent human brain, left hemisphere with Broca's area glowing warm orange, neural pathways as thin glowing filaments, glossy tissue shader.
character_sheet_descriptions.kid_turnaround: Stylized 3D girl around 8 years old, curly black hair in two puffs, yellow hoodie, denim overalls, big curious eyes, smooth plasticine skin with subtle subsurface scattering.

beats.narration: If every human on Earth suddenly lost the ability to speak... the silence wouldn't be the scariest part.

shots.scene_description: Stylized 3D man standing on a busy miniature city street, mouth wide open trying to shout, but nothing comes out; surrounding 3D pedestrians freeze clutching their throats in confusion.
Extreme close-up of the man's face, eyes wide in panic, hands gripping his throat, dramatic red rim light.

beats.narration: Inside your throat, two tiny folds of muscle that normally vibrate hundreds of times a second would simply... stop.

shots.scene_description: Anatomical 3D cutaway of the man's neck revealing the larynx, the camera diving down the glossy pink airway toward the vocal folds.
Top-down macro of the two pearly-white vocal folds rapidly vibrating with blurred motion lines, then abruptly freezing still as air rushes silently past them.

beats.narration: Within minutes, emergency calls go dead quiet, and air traffic control can't talk down a single plane.

shots.scene_description: Stylized 3D emergency dispatcher at a glowing console holding a headset, a caller's sound waveform on the screen flatlining.
Miniature 3D airport at dusk with toy-like jets stacked in circling holding patterns above a control tower, red warning lights blinking.

beats.narration: But your brain wouldn't give up. The same region that builds spoken sentences also powers sign language.

shots.scene_description: Semi-translucent 3D cutaway of the man's head, Broca's area on the left side of the brain glowing bright orange.
Glowing orange neural signals racing from Broca's area down through the spinal cord and along the arm into the man's fingers, which light up as they form a hand shape.

beats.narration: And kids would adapt fastest. In the 1980s, deaf children in Nicaragua invented a brand-new sign language almost from scratch.

shots.scene_description: Stylized 3D schoolyard with a group of kids, led by the girl in the yellow hoodie, animatedly signing to each other with big expressive hand shapes and laughing.
Close-up of the girl's hands forming a sign, soft glowing trails following her fingers, warm golden key light.

beats.narration: So humanity wouldn't stay silent for long... we'd just start talking with our hands.

shots.scene_description: The man and the girl on the now-calm city street, both smiling and signing to each other while pedestrians around them sign too, bright warm studio lighting.
